reasoning.text: The render reads clearly as an FPGA NTT accelerator — TOP shows eight blue BRAM banks, copper DSP multiplier cylinders, the reduction spine and the right-edge twiddle/addr/controller cluster, and SIDE confirms the exploded butterfly cluster floats correctly on risers above the array. But the headline 8-parallel-BU configuration is still only half-built: the render shows just four butterfly rows, costing structural-decomposition and proportional points the prior pass flagged twice. The two reduction members are still indistinguishable opaque boxes in TOP, and there is no visible operand-return routing from the registers back to the crossbar, so the dataflow loop reads as open-ended.
gaps: Eight clusters at 1.1 m pitch make the central array dense; verify in the next render that the copper multipliers and add/sub blocks are not mutually occluded in ISO, and if so widen vertical separation or stagger multiplier heights
The operand-return bus is a single straight bar; consider explicit arrowhead/cone geometry at the crossbar end so direction of return (reduction -> crossbar) is unambiguous rather than just a span

The exploded cluster still only explodes one of eight BUs; a faint second ghost outline or a small '×8' label-block could communicate that all eight lanes are identical instances of the exploded datapath

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) For each of the four parallel butterfly clusters, lay an open baseplate, then populate it with a DSP modular multiplier, a symmetric modular adder, a symmetric modular subtractor, and a pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right of the clusters as two members: the Barrett q-multiplier first, then the shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register and returning to the crossbar. 6) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM (feeding all multipliers), the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller, and the clock PLL. 7) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array, and clamp the exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
meta.after: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Lay one shared open butterfly-array baseplate across the array, then populate it with eight parallel butterfly clusters (one per BRAM bank), each a DSP modular multiplier, a symmetric modular adder, a symmetric modular subtractor and a pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar to close the conflict-free read-modify-write loop. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM (feeding all multipliers), the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array, and clamp the exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
